questions.stem: A crew loader reads crews.csv with pd.read_csv and no dtype=. Its column shifts holds values like 2;3;1. The loader worked for a year. This week every crew in the file has a single shift, and df['shifts'].str.split(';') fails. What changed?

options.text: The file's format, since a column with no ';' is no longer a valid CSV column
options.says: The file is still valid CSV. What changed is the data in the column, and with it the type pandas guessed.

options.text: Nothing in the data, since read_csv gives a column the same type on every file
options.says: pandas guesses each column's type from what that file holds, so the same column can be text one week and integers the next.

options.text: The column's guessed type, since with no ';' left every cell reads as a number
options.says: Right: with only single numbers in it, the column is read as int64, and .str needs text. Passing dtype= fixes the type.

options.text: The whole table's type, since one numeric column turns every column into int64
options.says: Each column gets its own dtype; the other columns keep theirs. Only shifts changed.

origin.section: Read Each Column With the Type the Model Needs, Not the Type pandas Guesses

questions.stem: A crew-hours table is long: one row per crew and month, with integer hours, and some crews have no row for some months. An analyst pivots it so months become columns before handing it to the model. What fills a crew's missing months in the pivoted table?

options.text: NaN, and every month column that holds one turns from integers into floats
options.says: Right: a pair with no row has nothing to put in its cell, so pandas writes NaN, and a column with NaN cannot be int64.

options.text: Zero, and every month column keeps the integer hours of the long table
options.says: pandas does not invent a zero for a missing pair; it marks the cell NaN, which turns the column into floats.

options.text: Empty text, and every month column that holds one turns into strings
options.says: A missing cell becomes NaN, pandas' marker for a missing value, not an empty string.

options.text: Nothing, since the pivot drops each crew that is missing any month
options.says: The pivot keeps every crew as a row and fills its missing months with NaN.

origin.section: Turn Each Table Into the Sets and Dicts the Model Indexes

questions.stem: An asset export lists transformer T-17 twice, once with a cost of 820 and once with 860. Apart from that, both rows pass every check. What should the loader do with them?

options.text: Keep the first row, since an export lists the newer value of a record first
options.says: Nothing tells the loader which copy is newer or right; keeping one is a guess the planners never see.

options.text: Keep the cheaper row, since the lower cost makes the plan the safer one
options.says: Choosing a cost is a guess, and the model will then defend a plan built on it as optimal.

options.text: Keep one row with the mean cost, since the average splits the difference
options.says: A repaired number is still a number nobody wrote; the loader rejects rather than repairs.

options.text: Reject both rows, since the loader cannot tell which of the two is right
options.says: Right: duplicated(keep=False) marks every copy, and both go back to the planners to settle.

origin.section: Check Every Row Before the Model Sees It, One Mask per Rule
